slides.title: Self-train YOLO
slides.subtitle: feature map first, then NV12
slides.notes: Chapter 2 Model Zoo, lesson 5: self-train YOLO—tune the quantization path with feature map first, then switch to NV12. Model is YOLO11n detect; dataset is the public mini-set coco128. Dual boards: X5 and S100. [Read] YOLO as yolo; feature map as a whole word; NV12 per handbook.

slides.title: Lesson Goals
slides.heading: Leave able to ==ship== this path
slides.lead: Self-train detect → feature map on both boards → then NV12 → one Sample frame.

slides.heading: Principle & yaml
slides.notes: Part two: why every model starts with feature map, and get the conversion yaml right.

slides.title: Why Feature Map First
slides.heading: Every model ==first== tunes with feature map
slides.caption: Once the full path works, then consider NV12 or RGB

scene.text: feature map first, then change the input protocol
When the path fails, hard to tell quant vs preprocess

scene.label: No color / normalize vars · cal = real input

scene.text: Same 0..1 domain: compare ONNX vs quant per board file
Once it works, switch to NV12 or RGB

steps.caption: If you compile NV12 or RGB first: cal must pass color space and normalize
With many variables, a broken path hides whether it is quant or preprocess
So every model starts with feature map: cal data is the model’s true input tensor
Both FM boards use 0..1: X5 .rgbchw, S100 .npy; compare ONNX vs quant with that board’s file—containers differ, do not mix
Once the full path works, then consider NV12 or RGB

slides.notes: Left: jumping to NV12 or RGB forces cal through color and normalize—too many variables when the path fails. Right: feature map is the float32 input tensor fed to the network, matching the self-train ONNX domain of zero-to-one. Both boards share that numeric domain; only the container differs—X5 .rgbchw, S100 .npy. Compare with that board’s file; do not mix. This is a single-image input-domain loop, not an mAP or generalization accuracy cert. Once it works, switch to NV12 or RGB. [Read] feature map whole word; NV12 per handbook; YOLO as yolo.

slides.title: What FM Means
slides.heading: OE featuremap is ==not== a mid-layer
slides.lead: Here featuremap = the float32 tensor fed straight into the network, matching the ONNX input.

items.text: Matches real network input—easy ONNX↔quant compare
Not a CNN mid-layer feature map; then change NV12/RGB protocol

slides.notes: OE featuremap is the float32 tensor fed straight into the network—not a CNN mid-layer. Cal matches real network input for compare; change the input protocol only after it works. [Read] feature map whole word.

slides.title: Input Protocol
slides.heading: rt meets the edge · train is the ==input domain==
slides.lead: train does not mean “train again”: it is the float model’s input domain; rt is what the board actually feeds.

items.text: train_*: float model input (FM=featuremap; NV12 stage=rgb)
Keep dtype/layout apart from color protocol: NV12 ≠ RGB layout

slides.notes: Input protocol: train describes the float model input domain—not retraining; rt describes what the board actually feeds. In the feature-map stage both sides are featuremap; in the NV12 stage rt becomes nv12 and train becomes rgb. RGB and NV12 are different input protocols. See X5 / S OE docs.

slides.title: Sample Hard Limit
slides.heading: Stock Sample ==NV12 only==
slides.lead: A feature-map Model Zoo artifact will not drop into the stock ultralytics_yolo runtime—use other verify tools.

items.text: FM artifact → stock Sample: will not connect
Legacy APIs are weak on featuremap · details in 2-06

slides.notes: Hard limit must be said: do not drop a feature-map artifact into stock Sample; on board use hrt_model_exec or hbm_runtime; inference API details are left for two-point-oh-six.

slides.title: X5-FM On Board
slides.heading: model_info + ==one-frame infer==
slides.lead: On board, only write under /tmp/course_2-05/. NEW: feed /255 only; Infer 31.316 ms; six heads vs ORT cosine ≥0.991; 8 dets.
slides.notes: X5 feature map on board. model_info should show input F32 from DDR. This round’s PR19 rebuild, fed divide-by-two-fifty-five only: Infer thirty-one point three one six milliseconds; all six heads vs ORT cosine at least zero point nine nine one; decode yields eight detections on the same image and thresholds as ORT. This is a single-image input-domain loop, not an mAP or full accuracy verification. The old twenty-six point seven three nine millisecond anchor was the pre-fix zero-to-two-fifty-five cal domain—do not present it as current FM.

slides.title: Three Fields → NV12
slides.heading: From feature map ==change three==
slides.caption: Swap cal, re-run OE; once green, remaining gaps should mostly be preprocess

scene.text: feature map → NV12: change three fields
Swap cal, re-run OE; gaps should mostly be preprocess

steps.caption: Recall feature map: types, layout, no_preprocess, per-board float32 cal
Field 3: norm_type → scale preprocess, and swap the image cal pipeline
On both boards: X5 is packed NV12; S100 is Y and UV split
Swap cal, re-run OE; once green, remaining gaps should mostly be preprocess

slides.notes: First recall feature map: types, layout, no preprocess, float32 calibration. Field 1: input_type_rt to nv12. Field 2: input_type_train to rgb. Field 3: norm to data_scale, and swap the calibration images. X5 is packed NV12; S100 is Y and UV split. After the change, swap calibration and re-run OE; once it works, remaining gaps should mostly be preprocess. YAML fields follow conversion/. [Read] NV12—never NVR; bayes-e / nash-e = arch + pause + letter.

slides.title: YAML · NV12 Side-by-side
slides.heading: Use ==data_scale== ≈1/255 · cal per board
slides.lead: ptq_nv12_{x5,s100}.yaml; YAML data_scale≈1/255 (not mean+scale). X5 on-disk 0..255 + mapper HzPreprocess; S100 on-disk /255, calibrate sees 0..1, then insert_image_preprocess at quantize—data_scale is for runtime, not a second /255.
head: Item
X5 NV12
S100 NV12
slides.notes: NV12 side-by-side: rt to nv12, train to rgb; YAML uses data_scale about one over two-fifty-five—not data_mean_and_scale. X5: on-disk zero-to-two-fifty-five rgbchw, then mapper HzPreprocess. S100: on-disk already /255 npy; compile calibrates on 0..1, then inserts image preprocess at quantize; YAML data_scale is for runtime—not a second divide at cal time. Do not reuse the old X5 featuremap zero-to-two-fifty-five story for NV12 or FM. X5 packed; S100 Y+UV. YAML follows conversion/. [Read] NV12—never NVR.

slides.title: X5-NV12 Compile
slides.heading: Rebuild · name contains ==nv12==
slides.lead: X5 uses packed NV12; cal switches to the image pipeline.
slides.notes: Round three: X5 NV12 compile. Three fields changed; prefix carries selftrain and nv12; X5 is packed single-stream NV12 input.

slides.heading: Back into ==ultralytics_yolo==

slides.notes: X5 back to Sample. Stock Sample accepts NV12 artifacts; this lesson’s board run on bus yields five detections. Sample pre/post changes are for later lessons—this lesson only needs one frame green.

slides.notes: Round four: S100 NV12 compile. Versus X5: S100 is two-stream Y and UV split, with a full recompile.
